session_cue.text: "Ow, why did you do that?" - Squints

previous.text: Trout recruited Squints, a newly arrived halfling, into his Halfling Corps as a junior assistant.
Dunk spied a magical mithril chain shirt through the window of Warwick the smith's shop.
Dunk struck a secret deal with Ingrid the alchemist and brought her diluted faun wine for a sleeping potion.
The party caught Naggeneen the Clurichen drinking the Golden Egg's alcohol and handed him to Quinn.
Father William accused Dr. Uriah of seeking profit from the dragon and measured him for webbing.
George the Hunter told Sir Phidipaldi the dragon's lair lies north, at the foot of the mountains.
At Trout's lead, the party set out through the forest for Brandon's Barrow Mound to seek its sword.
Dunk outdrank the fauns and traded a rabbit's foot for a flask of their wine.
Dr. Uriah joined Ingrid in criticizing Father William, and she said hidden fairies are appearing more often.
Squints pulled Brother Dirk from a sleeping giant's cottage, and the party outran the waking giant. Trout's sling shot hit Squints instead.

current.where_you_are: The party is in the woods north of Brandonsford, across the field from the giant's stone cottage. Squints and the rescued Brother Dirk are with them.

immediate_intention.text: The party is still headed to the Barrow. They are pressing Brother Dirk to come along instead of going home, and Trout has told him he now reports to Squints.

Your goals.text: Kill the black dragon and drag its body into Brandonsford to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000-gold bounty.
Get Warwick the smith's mithril chain shirt.

Standing in your way.text: George says nothing pierces the black dragon's scales, which blocks killing it. His companions' arrows and swords all failed.
Farmer Gill says Warwick displays his mithril chain shirt but always refuses to sell it.

What could help.text: Father William says that if the party retrieves Brandon's sword from the Barrow Mound, they will have the one weapon that can kill the dragon. George says no one knows if this is true or where the sword is.
If Dunk gives Warwick Ingrid's finished sleeping potion, it could keep Warwick asleep while Dunk is inside his house.
If the party pays Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter, she will join them against the dragon.
Dunk says that if he gets Warwick's magical mithril chain shirt, it could help against the dragon.

Still unanswered.text: Why has nothing reached Brandonsford in months?

Promises and debts.text: Dunk must help Ingrid get into Warwick's house and give Warwick her sleeping potion. Dunk said he would see her tonight.
Dr. Uriah owes Father William penance at Brandon's Barrow Mound and 10 gold for the Mound's upkeep.
Trout owes Squints second pick of the party's first treasure, after the elite members pick.

Meanwhile.text: The black dragon's bite kills, and it may kill those who confront it, including Farmer Gill's three sons.
George says the black dragon cannot fly yet but soon will, and then they're doomed.
The giant who meant to eat Brother Dirk is now awake, and its stone cottage lies on the way to the Barrow.

threads.name: The treasure map
threads.note: Father William marked the witch's home and the Barrow Mound on the map (beat_46), and the party will check a marked location on the way (beat_69), but the treasure is still unfound.

threads.name: The Clurichen of the riverbanks
threads.note: The question is answered: the Clurichen, Naggeneen, was drinking the Golden Egg's alcohol (beat_33). He is captured but not gone, hanging in a bag behind Quinn's bar (beat_34, beat_35), and he offered a pot of gold or a secret for his release.

threads.name: The black dragon near Brandonsford
threads.note: The lair's location is now known (beat_50). The danger sharpened: the dragon is poisonous, its scales are unpierceable and it will soon fly. The hunt now hinges on Brandon's magic sword (beat_42), and the bounty's payment is in doubt (beat_52).

threads.name: Hiring Lady Hilda
threads.note: Lady Hilda was only seen this Session. Sir Phidipaldi's promise to come back and hire her is unreleased.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer
threads.note: Ned was only seen this Session, and his offer was not taken up or declined.

threads.name: The missing shipments to Brandonsford
threads.note: Shipments still have not come in, and the cause is unknown.

threads.name: Sir Phidipaldi's quarrel with Eric the Reeve
threads.note: Eric never accepted the challenge, and the dawn passed with no duel. Sir Phidipaldi's continued disdain (beat_52) does not renew it, and nothing is owed.

threads.name: Shamus the mule
threads.note: Gill will lower Shamus's price once his sons return (beat_3), but Dunk has not yet got the mule.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Dunk scouted the shirt and Warwick's open window (beat_12) and says he has a plan to get it (beat_65), but he does not have it yet.

threads.name: Quinn's vanishing ale
threads.note: The ale thief was found to be Naggeneen, not Bentley (beat_33), and Quinn paid the party (beat_34). Nothing remains open.

threads.name: Trout's Halfling Corps
threads.note: Squints joined under Trout's terms, including second pick of the first treasure (beat_38), and Brother Dirk now reports to Squints (beat_81). The recruits' standing and the promised share remain open.

threads.name: Dunk's sleeping-potion deal with Ingrid
threads.note: Dunk supplied diluted faun wine for a sleeping potion that he will help Ingrid give to Warwick, and the potion and their next meeting are still pending (beat_71). It serves Dunk's stated plan to get Warwick's armor (beat_25, beat_65).

threads.name: Brandon's magic sword
threads.note: Father William says the dragon cannot be killed without the sword buried with Brandon (beat_42), which gives it a stated purpose. The party is heading to the Barrow to get it (beat_69).

threads.name: Dr. Uriah's penance at the Barrow Mound
threads.note: Dr. Uriah promised Father William to do penance at the Barrow Mound and donate 10 gold, and he has not yet done so.

threads.name: The giant in the woods
threads.note: The party rescued Brother Dirk and outran the giant (beat_78). The giant is awake, angry and still on the road to the Barrow, so the danger has not ended.

facts.text: Find the treasure.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations they do not recognize.

classification.support_basis: The map is the party's only guide to the treasure, though they cannot yet match most of its marked locations to the land.

facts.text: Where is the treasure?

classification.grounding_justification: The map marks several unrecognized locations and the party only assumes the treasure is at one of them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it means identifying a location, a fairly direct discovery.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental to finding the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Matching unknown map locations to unfamiliar land plausibly involves exploring and asking locals.

facts.text: The party plans to check a location marked on the treasure map that lies on their route through the forest to the Barrow.

classification.support_basis: Checking a marked site could reveal whether the treasure is there, but nothing establishes that this particular mark holds it.
classification.action_basis: The party agreed to stop at the marked location on the way to the Barrow, a physically available detour.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: visiting the marked site en route. Benefit: searching a candidate treasure site, which is simply pursuing the want itself rather than a distinct advantage.

facts.text: Where did the treasure map come from?

classification.grounding_justification: Dr. Uriah tried and failed to recall anything of the map's history, loosely raising the question.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Its origin could reveal who made it and why, but nothing suggests a hidden situation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: No leads or sources about the map's history are established.

facts.text: What is the Clurichen up to when it comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night?
facts.ended_how: answered: the Clurichen, Naggeneen, was drinking the Golden Egg's alcohol

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald explicitly says a trickster creature enters town nightly and is up to no good, without saying what it does; Sir Phidipaldi's account of it was shown wrong.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the hidden activity and intentions of a creature that visits town nightly.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning what the trickster does could explain strange happenings in a town with several unexplained troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Its nightly route from the riverbanks into town could be watched, followed or asked about.

facts.text: Reginald the Frog warns that the Clurichen, a trickster up to no good, comes into town every night and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.
facts.ended_how: removed: Naggeneen was captured and hangs in a bag behind Quinn's bar

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The creature is only said to be a trickster up to no good; no specific harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Trickery is implied, with nothing suggesting serious injury.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on the testimony of a single talking frog, not otherwise confirmed.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald describes a nightly pattern of visits into town, but no concrete harm linked to it.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can heed the warning and avoid where it goes, though they don't know where that is.

facts.text: Naggeneen, the Clurichen hanging captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar at the Golden Egg, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever lets him go.

classification.support_basis: A pot of gold or an unspecified secret has no established connection to any want or debt of the party.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen offered the terms himself, but he is now Quinn's captive behind the bar, so releasing him would need access or Quinn's cooperation that play has not established.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: releasing Naggeneen from his bag. Benefit: his pot of gold or a secret, with no specific advantage toward any established want or debt.

facts.resource_subject: Naggeneen captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar

facts.text: What does Quinn intend to do with the captive Naggeneen?

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn pointedly says he knows what he will do with Naggeneen without saying what, and the bag still hangs behind the bar the next morning.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single statement from Quinn would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting about the fate of a captured fairy, mainly local.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Quinn is immediately available to ask.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000-gold bounty.
Where is the black dragon near Brandonsford?
facts.ended_how: answered: George says its lair is north at the foot of the mountains (replaced by fact_new_1)

classification.grounding_justification: The dragon is only rumored and said to be 'outside town'; its location is a clear gap the hunt depends on.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single discovery, such as George's account or tracking, would likely settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental for finding and killing the dragon.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Witnesses George and Gill and the sons' hunt offer leads to follow.

facts.text: Where did this new dragon come from, given Sir Brandon's dragon was killed centuries ago?

classification.grounding_justification: Gill and Bentley note nothing like this has happened since Sir Brandon's dragon died, and Gill says he doesn't know where dragons come from.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer could reveal a hidden cause behind the dragon's appearance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could tie the present dragon to the town's legend.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The legend offers some lore to follow, but no concrete leads.

facts.text: The black dragon outside Brandonsford, whose poisonous bite kills and which killed George's companions at its lair, may kill those who confront it, including Farmer Gill's three sons, who are hunting it.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Death by poisoned bite to those who confront it, shown by George's dead companions and lost arm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George, a survivor, gives a firsthand account of the dragon killing his friends.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Gill's sons are still hunting it, but no new attacks are reported.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could kill the dragon or warn the sons, though killing it needs the sword.

facts.text: Eric says the woodsman George, who met the dragon and lives a couple of houses down from the Clumsy Fox, may come to the tavern tonight; the party could ask him what he saw and where.
facts.ended_how: used up: Sir Phidipaldi questioned George

classification.support_basis: George is a firsthand witness who could help the party learn where the dragon is and what it is like, though he doesn't know where his arm went.
classification.action_basis: Eric told the party to ask George themselves and said where he lives.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: talking with George. Benefit: a firsthand account of the dragon and the encounter site, helping locate and face it.

facts.text: Lady Hilda's offer to join the party for pay could add a seasoned fighter to the dragon hunt.

classification.support_basis: An armored, seasoned ally would strengthen the party against the dragon, though she says she could not kill it herself.
classification.action_basis: Hilda offered to join adventurers for money, explicitly in the context of the dragon.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Hilda. Benefit: a seasoned armored fighter for the dragon fight.

facts.text: George says the dragon's lair is north at the foot of the mountains, with no climbing needed.

classification.support_basis: Knowing where the lair is lets the party find and confront the dragon.

facts.text: George says the black dragon cannot fly yet but soon will, and then, he says, they're doomed.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: George predicts doom once it flies, implying it would range freely and threaten the town, but the exact harm is unstated.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: A flying, deadly dragon would endanger many people.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on George's testimony as a survivor, without further confirmation.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George says the dragon will fly soon, an advancing process, though no timing is given.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon before it flies would prevent it, but that needs the sword.

facts.text: George says nothing pierces the black dragon's scales; his companions' arrows and swords all failed. This blocks killing the dragon.

classification.scope_basis: The scales are an inherent property of the dragon and will stop ordinary weapons in any fight with it.

facts.text: Brandon's magic sword at the Barrow Mound, which Father William says is needed to kill the dragon, could let the party kill it.

classification.support_basis: Father William says the dragon cannot be killed without it, so it would overcome the central obstacle, though no one knows the legend's truth.
classification.action_basis: The party has decided to go to the Barrow to get the sword.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: retrieving the sword from the Barrow. Benefit: a weapon said to be able to kill the otherwise unkillable dragon.

facts.resource_subject: Brandon's magic sword needed to kill the dragon

facts.text: Dunk says Warwick's magical mithril chain shirt, which he plans to get, could help against the dragon.

classification.support_basis: Magic armor could protect a fighter against the dragon, though whether it guards against its poison bite is unknown.
classification.action_basis: Dunk has a plan to get the shirt, and armor straightforwardly matches the need for protection in a fight.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: obtaining the shirt. Benefit: magical protection for a fighter facing the dragon.

facts.resource_subject: Warwick's glowing magical mithril chain shirt

facts.text: Does Eric the Reeve actually have the 1000 gold he promised for the dragon?

classification.grounding_justification: George explicitly doubts Eric has the money.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A bounded fact about Eric's funds.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly practical for the reward, mildly interesting given Eric's character.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked by asking Eric or townsfolk.

facts.text: George allows that Sir Phidipaldi's lance may be one of the few weapons not yet tried on the dragon.

classification.support_basis: An untried weapon offers a slim chance against the scales, but nothing suggests it will pierce them.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George to bring his lance against the dragon.

classification.stake_basis: No evidence George relies on or has a claim to Phidipaldi using his lance; it is a statement of intent after George's remark.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter with chain mail and a shield, offers to join a party of adventurers against the dragon for pay; she says she cannot kill it herself.

classification.support_basis: A more seasoned armored fighter would strengthen the party's attempt to kill the dragon for the Reeve's bounty, though her fee is unset and she says she cannot kill it alone.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join an adventuring party against the dragon for money, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would return to hire her.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: paying Hilda to join; benefit: an experienced armored fighter added to the party's dragon hunt. Linked by her own offer.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk with the Reeve and come back to hire her.

classification.stake_basis: This is a stated intention to return and hire her; no evidence shows Hilda relies on or has a claim to the party coming back.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold for the week, on condition that he gets to kill people with the wasp; he would give back 5 gold per killing he is allowed if he can do what he wants with the victims. Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

classification.support_basis: Ned would add a hired killer with a fast-killing wasp, but play established no specific want or debt of the party that his services would serve.
classification.action_basis: Ned did offer the terms, but no established want or debt of the party is linked to hiring him, so the concrete advantage would be invented.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: paying Ned 100 gold to hire him and his wasp. Benefit: an extra killer, but no specific advantage toward any established want or debt was established.

facts.text: What is Drop Dead Ned's killer wasp?

classification.grounding_justification: Ned calls it a killer wasp kept in a jar, but Dr. Uriah sensed nothing unusual about it, so the question is only loosely suggested.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying the creature's nature is a simple property.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little beyond examining the jar or asking Ned.

facts.text: Why has nothing reached Brandonsford in months, including Bentley's tavern restock shipment that was due a week ago?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley, Farmer Gill and Quinn all independently noted that shipments have stopped, Bentley called it unprecedented since Sir Brandon's time, and this Session the narration again stresses that shipments still haven't come in.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause behind a town-wide supply failure, possibly tied to other troubles in town.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining why the town has been cut off would change the party's understanding of Brandonsford's situation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could follow the supply route, question merchants such as Bentley and Warwick, or look for the missing shipment.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi wants to fight Eric the Reeve in the duel at dawn he challenged him to.
facts.ended_how: abandoned: Eric never accepted and the dawn passed with no duel; Sir Phidipaldi's continued disdain (beat_52) does not renew it

facts.text: Eric the Reeve has not accepted Sir Phidipaldi's duel challenge, only flusteredly saying Sir Phidipaldi is more skilled at adventure.
facts.ended_how: no longer relevant: the duel it blocked was abandoned when dawn passed

classification.scope_basis: Eric's refusal stands with no sign he will reconsider, so the duel cannot happen at dawn unless he changes his mind.

facts.text: Bentley forbids fighting at the Clumsy Fox and has ruled that Sir Phidipaldi must spend the night at the Golden Egg.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the night has passed and the duel it constrained was abandoned

classification.scope_basis: The ruling explicitly covers only this night, though the ban on fighting in his tavern may stand longer.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus, which Gill offers to sell for 100 gold.
Asked whether Dunk could trade work for Shamus, Farmer Gill says the big work needed is killing the dragon outside town; no trade was agreed, and Gill's three sons are already trying to kill it.
facts.ended_how: lapsed: the trade was never agreed or renewed; Gill now ties a lower price to his sons' return instead
facts.uncertain_reason: Gill never explicitly agreed to give Shamus in exchange for killing the dragon.

classification.support_basis: It could let Dunk get Shamus without paying 100 gold, but Gill never confirmed the trade and his sons may kill the dragon first.
classification.action_basis: Gill named dragon-killing as the work needed in reply to Dunk's question, but did not agree to exchange the mule for it.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: kill the dragon as work for Gill; benefit: obtaining Shamus in place of the 100-gold price. This is paying the want's own price in another form.

facts.text: Farmer Gill won't lower Shamus's price until his sons return from hunting the dragon, since he can't get work done without his boys or a mule.

classification.scope_basis: Gill states a standing condition tied to his sons' return, which lasts until they come back, beyond this conversation.

facts.text: Get Warwick the smith's mithril chain shirt.
facts.classification_change_basis: Previously the party had only heard of the shirt and never expressed wanting it (uncertain, incidental). This Session Dunk scouted it at night, found it clearly magical (beat_12), told the party it could help against the dragon and said he has a plan to get it (beat_65), with a whole sub-plot pursued toward it; this is now a confirmed, meaningful side pursuit.

facts.text: Farmer Gill says Warwick the smith displays his mithril chain shirt but always refuses to sell it.

classification.scope_basis: Gill describes Warwick's refusal as standing practice (he always refuses to sell), not a single encounter.

facts.text: Dunk knows the mithril chain shirt is kept in Warwick's shop, which adjoins his home; it glows in the moonlight and is clearly magical.

classification.support_basis: Knowing exactly where the shirt is kept lets Dunk plan a night entry to take it.

facts.resource_subject: Warwick's glowing magical mithril chain shirt

facts.text: Warwick's cracked-open bedroom window (thread_12) offers a way into his house to reach the shirt.

classification.support_basis: An open window gives entry to the house where the shirt is kept, though Warwick sleeps in that room.
classification.action_basis: Dunk observed the window left cracked open; climbing in is a supported physical option giving access to the shirt.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: entering through the open bedroom window at night. Benefit: access inside Warwick's locked home and shop to the shirt. Evidence: beat_12 shows the window left cracked open.

facts.text: What magic does Warwick's mithril chain shirt hold?

classification.grounding_justification: The shirt glows in the moonlight and is called clearly magical, but its powers are never described.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying an item's property is a simple fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental, whether it helps against the dragon.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by examining or identifying the item.

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for stealing his ale at night, and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
facts.ended_how: achieved: the thief proved to be Naggeneen, not Bentley, and Quinn paid Sir Phidipaldi, Trout and Dr. Uriah 33 gold each

facts.text: Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi plan a fake shipment: Quinn brings bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale to see who comes for it.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the thief was caught in the basement without the fake shipment

classification.support_basis: A conspicuous decoy delivery could draw out whoever takes Quinn's stock, giving a way to catch or identify the thief, though whether it works is untested.
classification.action_basis: Quinn proposed the plan and Sir Phidipaldi agreed to its terms, with Quinn supplying the bottles.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: staging the fake delivery. Benefit: luring the night thief into revealing themselves, advancing Quinn's job. Linked by Quinn's stated purpose of seeing what happens.

facts.text: Who or what empties and knocks over Quinn's stock each night?
facts.ended_how: answered: Naggeneen the Clurichen was drinking the Golden Egg's alcohol

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn explicitly describes a recurring nightly mystery of emptied and knocked-over glasses, with only his suspicion of Bentley.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden culprit and motive behind a repeated pattern.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the culprit would explain the tavern rivalry and could overturn Quinn's accusation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Supports stakeouts, the decoy shipment and questioning Bentley.

facts.text: Trout owes Squints second pick of the party's first treasure, after the elite members pick, in exchange for Squints joining the Halfling Corps under Trout's orders and funding himself and his gear until then.

classification.stake_basis: Squints joined and funds himself on the explicit promise of second pick, and came to town seeking his big break, so the share is what he relies on for his service.

facts.text: Squints, a halfling more experienced in fighting than Trout and armed with a sling and dagger, travels with the party as Trout's junior assistant under his orders.

classification.support_basis: An extra capable fighter accompanying the party toward the Barrow adds modest strength and an expendable scout, as shown when he retrieved the sack from the giant's cottage.

facts.text: Dunk has agreed to help Ingrid get into Warwick's house and give Warwick the sleeping potion she is making from the faun wine Dunk supplied, so she can watch him without waking him. Ingrid told Dunk to come back tomorrow; Dunk said he would see her tonight.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid's dearest wish is to watch Warwick without the fear of him waking, and she is making the potion relying on Dunk's offer to get her in and administer it.

facts.text: Once Ingrid finishes it, the sleeping potion she is making from the faun wine could keep Warwick asleep while Dunk is inside his house with her.

classification.support_basis: A sleeping Warwick would let Dunk be in the house near the glowing chain shirt without being caught, though the heavily diluted wine and doubts about Ingrid's skill leave its strength uncertain.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion and have Dunk help administer it inside Warwick's house; Dunk told the party he had a plan to get the armor.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: collect the finished potion from Ingrid and give it to Warwick. Benefit: Warwick stays asleep while Dunk is inside his house, removing the risk of waking him.

facts.text: Warwick sleeps in a second-story bedroom whose window is left cracked open; Ingrid climbs up to it every night.

classification.support_basis: The open window gives a way into Warwick's house to bring Ingrid in and administer the potion, and the tall Dunk can lift her up to it.
classification.action_basis: Dunk saw the cracked window and Ingrid already climbs to it nightly and asked tall Dunk to help reach it.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: climb or lift someone through the cracked window. Benefit: entry into Warwick's bedroom without forcing the locked shop.

facts.text: Will Ingrid's sleeping potion work, given the heavily diluted faun wine and Father William's claim that she can't make her own potions?

classification.grounding_justification: Dunk diluted the key ingredient to about 20%, and Father William and Ingrid contradict each other about whether she makes her potions herself.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Mostly a bounded question of whether the potion is effective, with a side question of Ingrid's real skill.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental to the plan, though Ingrid's competence touches the William-Ingrid rivalry.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked by testing the potion or asking Ingrid or Vivian, little more.

facts.text: Father William says the black dragon cannot be killed without the magic sword buried with Brandon in Brandon's Barrow Mound; the party could retrieve it from the Barrow.

classification.support_basis: Per Father William the sword is the only way to kill the dragon, whose scales nothing else has pierced, though George says no one knows what is true or where the sword is.
classification.action_basis: The party knows where the Barrow is and decided to walk there to get the sword; Brother Dirk was also heading there for it.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: retrieving the sword from the Barrow. Benefit: a weapon Father William says is required to kill the dragon, overcoming its unpierceable scales.

facts.resource_subject: Brandon's magic sword needed to kill the dragon

facts.text: Brandon's Barrow Mound is roughly a three-mile walk north through the forest, and Father William marked it on Dr. Uriah's map.

classification.support_basis: Knowing where the Barrow is lets the party reach the sword needed against the dragon; the distance estimate changed from a day's walk to about three miles.

facts.resource_subject: Location and distance of Brandon's Barrow Mound

facts.text: Does Brandon's magic sword really lie in the Barrow Mound?

classification.grounding_justification: Father William says the sword is buried with Brandon, while George says no one knows what is true or where the sword is.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Visiting the Barrow would largely settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental, though it bears on the truth of the Brandon legend.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Farmer Gill's fairytales and the Barrow itself offer some leads.

facts.text: George says Farmer Gill knows the fairytales of Sir Brandon and his magic sword; the party could ask Gill what they tell about the sword.

classification.support_basis: The tales might clarify the sword's nature or whereabouts, but George says no one knows what is true.
classification.action_basis: Dunk is on friendly terms with Farmer Gill and George names him as knowing the tales; no specific information is promised.
classification.opening_basis: Trigger: asking Farmer Gill about the Brandon fairytales. Benefit: possibly learning about the sword's origin or location, only vaguely established.

facts.text: Will Brother Dirk go home or continue to the Barrow for the sword?

classification.grounding_justification: Dirk said he should just go home, Sir Phidipaldi objected and Uriah invoked Father William, leaving his choice unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A simple decision by one person.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Routine; mainly whether he joins or leaves.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah owes Father William penance at Brandon's Barrow Mound and a donation of 10 gold for the Mound's upkeep.

classification.stake_basis: Father William specifically asked for this penance and donation for the Mound's upkeep, and Uriah agreed, so William has a direct claim on this act; his stake beyond the upkeep money is mostly religious and personal.

facts.text: The giant who captured Brother Dirk to eat him in a stew lives in a huge stone cottage in a clearing in the woods north of Brandonsford, on the way to the Barrow; it is awake after the party took its captive.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Dirk says the giant captures travellers and was going to eat him in a stew, a specific harm.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Being captured and eaten is death.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The party saw the giant and its bound captive, and Dirk testified to its intent, though whether it will strike at the party again is not shown.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The giant is awake and its cottage lies near the forest route the party and Dirk use to the Barrow, but no pursuit or new attack is shown; it tired and gave up the chase.
classification.preventability_justification: The party knows where the cottage is and easily outran the slow giant, so it can avoid or evade it.
